newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Gallop becomes W.Australia opposition leader.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Gallop becomes W.Australia opposition leader.

text.p: The Western Australian Labor Party on Tuesday voted in a new leader, Geoff Gallop, to replace Jim McGinty who said he thought Gallop could do a better job communicating the Labor Party's message to the electorate.
Gallop is the party's former deputy leader and shadow minister for health public sector management and accountability.
McGinty will take over as the deputy leader.

At a press conference in Perth, McGinty said he raised the leadership issue himself with Gallop after coming to the view that he had been unable to effectively communicate the Labor Party's message to the electorate.

"There are no internal problems (in the Labor Party) at all," McGinty said. "It was my idea. It was a decision taken with the best interests of the party at heart. There was no one tapping me on the shoulder suggesting I should go."
Later, Gallop said one of his first jobs would be to transfer his shadow portfolios to McGinty but he gave no indication of any other shadow cabinet reshuffle.
Gallop described the record of the state government led by Liberal Richard Court as "a dead end street"
But he acknowledged that Labor would have difficulty winning the next election.
"I've been in politics a long time," Gallop said.
"I know a difficult circumstance when I can see one and we've certainly got one today in Western Australia," he said.
"We've got to be realistic about that," he added.
Asked about whether he would try to reposition the party, Gallop said there was a need to "rethink" the balance between microeconomic reform and social justice.
"The ordinary West Australian families no longer have the security to build their families and participate in the community," Gallop said.
"They're frightened. They don't know if they will have a job tomorrow. If they do have a job it is on a very short term basis," he said.

"I think it is incumbent on all of us in politics to respond to that difficulty and develop a new concept of how we can organise our work place so that there is not only more justice but more security for workers," he said.
Gallop is a former Rhodes scholarship winner who joined the Labor Party in 1971.
He has a Master of Philosopy degree from Murdoch University and a doctorate in philosopy from Oxford University.
He was elected a member of parliament n a by-election 1986 and became a minister for education in parliamentary reform in 1990.
